rubric.result: The objective promises three things and the diff produces all three. (a) 'serve the ranking of every clone of the root': routes.ts adds `router.get('/coverage', ...)` which calls `deps.coverage.run()`, and CoverageRanking.run() lists every clone through `deps.catalog.list()` and sorts with CoverageOrder. (b) 'under /api': the route hangs off the same Router that createApp mounts under '/api', so it inherits the same errorHandler as the other four. (c) 'in the same typed envelope as the four endpoints already there': CoveragePayload.of returns `{ coverage: CoverageEntryPayload[] }`, the same single-key envelope shape as `{ repos: await deps.catalog.list() }` on line 35 of the same file, and the entries are a declared interface rather than an untyped literal. Nothing in the objective is missing and the diff adds no behaviour beyond it.

The **TDD:** line names `test('GET /api/coverage ranks every clone of the root by line coverage')` over `createApp(deps)`, with two clones written in tmp and the literal payload array asserted. The diff has that test verbatim: it clones 'high' and 'low' under the tmp root, writes an istanbul summary into each (90/100 and 50/100), goes through `request(createApp(world.deps)).get('/api/coverage')` and asserts `response.body` with `toEqual` against the literal two-element array, high before low. The expected values match the code under test: LineCount.percentage() gives 90 and 50, source 'istanbul' is the first candidate of COVERAGE_CANDIDATES, and CoverageOrder puts the higher percentage first. `measuredAt: expect.any(String)` is the one non-literal cell and it could not be literal: it is the mtime of a file the test just wrote. The second named test, `test('GET /api/coverage carries no author name or email')`, is also present and does exactly what the line describes: it clones with COMMITS and asserts `JSON.stringify(response.body)).not.toContain(AUTHOR)` over the AUTHOR constant already in that file.

Compared name by name. Contract (server/src/api/coverage-payload.ts): `CoverageEntryPayload` in the diff declares id: string, state: CoverageState, percentage: number | null, lines: { covered: number; total: number } | null, source: CoverageFormat | null, measuredAt: string | null — the same six names, in the same order, with the same types as the brief. `CoveragePayload.of(ranked: RankedCoverage): { coverage: CoverageEntryPayload[] }` matches the declared static signature; CoverageState, CoverageFormat and RankedCoverage are imported from the modules that actually export them (coverage-reading.ts, coverage-format.ts, coverage-ranking.ts). Call site (server/src/api/routes.ts): the brief's two lines appear verbatim, `response.json(CoveragePayload.of(await deps.coverage.run()))`. Current state block (routes.ts 33-35): the '/repos' handler is untouched and the new route sits beside it. app.ts: `coverage: CoverageRanking` is added to AppDeps; `createDeps()` builds `new CoverageRanking({ catalog, artifacts: new ArtifactFiles(createCache<CoverageReading>(COVERAGE_CACHE_LIMIT)), order: new CoverageOrder() })` with `const COVERAGE_CACHE_LIMIT = 64` — the constant name, the value and the three named constructor keys are the ones the brief writes, the only difference being the explicit `<CoverageReading>` type argument, which is the same call. The two required-field files carry exactly one new field each, as the brief says they must.

Row by row, for the rows this diff bears on. Route: `GET /api/coverage` with body `{ coverage: [...] }` like /repos — implemented exactly. Formats: the payload's `source` is typed `CoverageFormat | null`, the three-member union, so no fourth format can be serialized. Metric: the payload reads `reading.lines.percentage()`, the covered/total rounded to one decimal, and never recomputes it. 'No candidate counts': state 'no-artifact' with every value null — the second branch of entryOf returns percentage, lines, source and measuredAt all null, and the second new test asserts exactly that literal entry. 'Artefact that is not its format': state 'unreadable-artifact' reaches the wire through the same branch, with `state` travelling beside the nulls so the two stay distinguishable, which is what the task text asks for. Measure date: `reading.measuredAt.toISOString()`, ISO 8601 mtime. Cache key and order of the ranking: decided in earlier tasks, this diff only wires them (catalog shared with the ranking, COVERAGE_CACHE_LIMIT = 64). Spanish only for UI copy: every identifier, comment and test name in this diff is English, and this task touches no UI. One row deserves a note rather than a finding: 'New server code lives under server/src/coverage/' and the new module is server/src/api/coverage-payload.ts. The plan itself put it there — **Files:**, the Contract block header and the Call site all name that exact path, and a script already checked the path against **Files:** — and architecture.md places a boundary model in infrastructure, beside the other API code. The implementer could not have satisfied both; that is a defect of the plan and the plan is not what I judge.

Exemplars. server/src/api/routes.ts: the new route copies the shape of '/repos' — one line, `response.json(...)` over an awaited dependency, no try/catch, so failures fall to the shared errorHandler like every other route. server/src/api/routes.test.ts: the three new tests are integration tests over `createApp(deps)` with the root, the settings file and every clone in tmp, exactly the idiom of the file. server/src/repos.ts: not re-implemented; the ranking reuses the catalog. The web/ exemplars have no subject: this task touches no web file.
Repo rules (AGENTS.md), all satisfied: every relative import in the diff carries the `.js` suffix; the tests live beside the code; the payload carries id, state, percentage, lines, source and measuredAt and no author name or email; nothing in the diff mutates a clone or fetches; web/ imports nothing from server/ because web/ is untouched.
ct's five documents.
- defects.md, rule by rule. (1) Closed vocabulary instead of loose strings and booleans: the subject is CoverageState, and it is carried, not collapsed — `state` travels to the wire beside the nulls rather than as a boolean 'measured?', which is what keeps no-artifact and unreadable-artifact apart for the UI. The dispatch, though, is `if (reading.state === 'measured') { ... } return { ...nulls }`: the second return is a catch-all for the rest of the vocabulary, and a fourth member would fall into it silently. Reported as a low finding; the sibling coverage-order.ts shows the exhaustive `switch` with no default that this file could have used. (2) No raw map as the return value of logic: no subject in the logic — CoverageRanking returns RankedCoverage and RepoCoverage, declared types, and the only plain object literal in the diff is CoveragePayload's return, which is the wire envelope produced by the boundary model in one step and never read by key afterwards. That is the legitimate case, not the defect. (3) Two fields that have to agree: no subject, and the shape avoids it — the absence lives in the type as `number | null` and as a member of CoverageState, with no sentinel: a clone with no artefact never reports 0 %, and there is no empty string or epoch date standing for 'unset'. (4) Errors named for what happens, not for where: no subject in this diff — it defines no error type, and the one it depends on, UnreadableArtifact, is named for what happens and is raised in an earlier task.
- style.md. coverage-payload.ts is a new module and is born conforming: no comments, no docstrings, English throughout, and every function hangs off the CoveragePayload type. The two host files it modifies, routes.ts and app.ts, are the repository's declared debt (free functions and docstrings everywhere) and the diff follows their style there, which is not a finding. One place does break the new-concept rule: `class CoverageArtifactFixture` is a new concept placed inside the old test file and it is born with a docstring. Reported as a low finding. Its placement is right — testing.md wants test helpers hanging off a test type in the module, not in a shared one.
- decisions.md. No business rule written twice: the percentage stays in LineCount, the order in CoverageOrder, the candidate list in ArtifactFiles, and the payload derives none of them. `COVERAGE_CACHE_LIMIT = 64` beside routes.ts's `CACHE_LIMIT = 64` is the idiom of a cache, not the same decision — no business change forces touching both — and the brief prescribed that exact constant anyway.
- architecture.md. Directions hold: coverage-payload.ts sits in infrastructure and imports types from the coverage modules, never the other way round; the conversion to the wire lives in this boundary model and not in the use case, which is what the task text demands; app.ts stays the only place that assembles the graph and injects catalog, artifacts and order by name through the constructor; the route does not translate anything itself.
- testing.md. The assertion is on the literal payload of the boundary, not on a model of it rebuilt in the test; the arrange is not built with the piece under test — the artefact is written with `writeFileSync` and `JSON.stringify`, not with IstanbulArtifact; the doubles in app.test.ts and errors.test.ts reject rather than answer a request nobody wrote (`readingOf: () => Promise.reject(new Error('not used'))`); the test names are sentences about what is guaranteed. The three new assertions could each fail for the reason their name gives: the ranking test would fail on order, on percentage and on source; the no-artifact test on any non-null cell; the identity test on any leak of AUTHOR into the body.
No clash between a **Verification:** command of this task and any of the five documents.

I read the touched files and the test files are routes.test.ts, app.test.ts and errors.test.ts. app.test.ts and errors.test.ts have no `-` lines at all (7 insertions each, no deletions). The only `-` lines inside a test file are in routes.test.ts, and they are the seven lines of `depsOverTheSameFiles` rewritten from an arrow expression into a block body so the `catalog` const can be shared with CoverageRanking: `catalog`, `settings`, `analysis` and `now` come back identical on the `+` side and only `coverage` is added. No assertion, case or test is removed, relaxed or rewritten, and the other deletions in the diff are outside test files (the doc comment of routes.ts, which said 'The four endpoints' and is no longer true, and the `catalog: createCatalog(...)` line of app.ts). Nothing here for this item to report.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code. Reverting the production side of this diff — the route in routes.ts and coverage-payload.ts — leaves the three new tests failing on `expect(response.status).toBe(200)`, because '/api/coverage' would answer 404. The values the tests assert come from production code and not from scaffolding: the percentages from LineCount.percentage(), 'istanbul' from ArtifactFiles' first candidate, the order from CoverageOrder, the nulls from the second branch of CoveragePayload.entryOf, and measuredAt from the real mtime of the file. The test scaffolding is confined to writing a real artefact on disk (CoverageArtifactFixture, with writeFileSync) and to real clones in tmp; the ArtifactFiles, CoverageRanking and CoverageOrder the router uses in routes.test.ts are the real instances, nothing is mocked on the coverage path, and no expected value is hard-coded in production code to satisfy a test.

Read inside the six declared files. Everything the diff writes answers a sentence of the task. coverage-payload.ts is the Contract block, nothing more — no extra export, no helper the contract does not name. routes.ts gains the Call site line and its import. app.ts gains the AppDeps field, COVERAGE_CACHE_LIMIT and the CoverageRanking assembly the task spells out; the `catalog` const it hoists is the mechanical consequence of the ranking needing the same catalog, and the `createCache` import the consequence of the assembly the task dictates. The doc-comment edit in routes.ts ('The four endpoints' → 'The endpoints ... Everything but /coverage') is the correction the new route forces on a sentence that would otherwise be false, in a file the task modifies. routes.test.ts gains the three tests the **Tests:** line lists and the fixture they need. app.test.ts and errors.test.ts gain one field each, as the brief says. No refactor, rename or adjacent fix rides along. Nothing from `### Out of scope` is present: nothing runs a test or a coverage tool inside a clone, nothing reads CI or an external service, and there is no history, trend, per-folder breakdown, threshold or traffic light.

Three new tests, all in routes.test.ts. Deterministic: no real clock or today's date inside an assertion (the one time-dependent cell, measuredAt, is asserted as `expect.any(String)`), no network, no path outside a temporary directory (the root comes from `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'repo-pulse-api-'))`), no randomness and no sleep. Isolated: `beforeEach` builds a fresh world with its own tmp directory and its own cache, `afterEach` calls `world.cleanup()`, and each of the three creates the clones it needs, so none depends on state another left nor on its position in the file — the second one can assert a single-entry array precisely because the root is empty when it starts. Verifies real behaviour: each assertion is on the HTTP response of `createApp(deps)` over real files on disk, not on a mock's call count, a stub's return value or a constant the test just defined, and each would fail with the production lines of this diff reverted (404 instead of 200). All three properties hold, so this item is conforme; I report nothing from the finer half, so the test-driven-development skill was not needed to pin a sentence.

findings.what: The dispatch over CoverageState in the new boundary model has a catch-all branch: `if (reading.state === 'measured')` returns the measured payload and the fallthrough `return` serves every other member. A fourth state would be serialized as all-nulls silently instead of failing visibly. The sibling module of this same slice, server/src/coverage/coverage-order.ts, shows the shape that does fail visibly: `switch (state)` with a case per member and no `default`. Low, not medium: the vocabulary is closed at three by a row of `## 2. Closed decisions`, and both non-measured members legitimately project to the same nulls, so nothing is wrong today.
findings.evidence: `conventions/defects.md`: "Dispatch over it exhaustively, with no catch-all branch, so that adding a member fails visibly" and, in its antipatterns, "A catch-all branch in a dispatch over a closed vocabulary." The line: `    return {` following `if (reading.state === 'measured') { ... }` with no per-member case.
